name: Room Addition Timeline in Los Angeles County: Design to Final Inspection

mainEntity.name: What timeline should I expect for a typical 400–600 sq ft room addition in Los Angeles County from design through final inspection?
mainEntity.text: What timeline should I expect for a typical 400–600 sq ft room addition in Los Angeles County from design through final inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 400–600 square foot room addition in Los Angeles County, a realistic start-to-finish timeline is usually 6–10 months. The front-end design and permitting phase often takes 2–4 months. This includes initial consultations, drafting plans, structural engineering, Title 24 calculations, and city plan-check reviews, plus any required resubmittals. Once permits are issued, construction typically runs 3–6 months. Early stages—demolition, foundation, and framing—move faster but are heavily dependent on inspections and weather. Rough plumbing, electrical, and HVAC follow, then insulation, drywall, and finishes. Delays often occur around inspection scheduling, late design changes, material backorders, and unexpected structural issues discovered once walls are opened. Final inspections and punch-list corrections take additional time, especially if there are multiple agencies involved (building, electrical, mechanical, fire, or public works). Your contractor should give you a written schedule with milestones and clarify which parts are within their control and which depend on city and utility response times. Ask potential contractors to share recent timelines for similar additions in your specific city, as some Los Angeles County jurisdictions have longer plan-check and inspection backlogs than others. Planning for a wider time window from the start reduces frustration and helps you time temporary living arrangements if needed.
